discovery: Apply every assigned criterion to every changed file and read the whole file. Report all independent supported defects; neither a minimum number of findings nor an empty result is a goal. Compare head/base to distinguish introduced defects, incomplete newly promised behavior, preexisting limitations and intentional changes. Read-only inspection of unchanged consumers is part of the review; the diff restricts report anchors, not evidence gathering. When changed behavior introduces or relies on implicit context, scoped state, inherited configuration or a cross-boundary guarantee, trace installation -> consumer -> execution/lifetime boundary -> actual use. Inspect relevant task/thread handoffs, queues, callbacks, lazy streams and cancellation/cleanup boundaries. A span, copied security context or suggestive type name does not prove that independent state is transferred. Follow real production consumers and their dispatch abstractions, not just references to the new helper. Keep a working list of concrete suspected broken guarantees and resolve it before declaring the pass complete. This is a draft source pass. A separate closure pass will inspect its claims and unresolved consumer paths before any successful checkpoint. Keep concrete incomplete paths in notes, including the next unresolved dispatch edge; do not silently replace a runtime hypothesis with a documentation suggestion. Emit internal boundary_obligations in the draft pass: an array of {id,hypothesis,next_edge}, with IDs <module>:chain:<index>. Include every concrete cross-boundary suspicion, including one not emitted as a finding because its consumer remains untraced; use [] only when none applies.
evidence: For a credible cross-file hypothesis, use the trusted nonstop_context find_symbol/find_references/search_code tools to locate consumers and implementations across the pinned repository, including unchanged code, then read the relevant units or full files. Start from the changed producer/consumer and narrow broad boundary searches by the related subsystem; inspect continuation or narrow a query when the first page contains unrelated hits or mostly declarations/mocks. References are lexical hints, not resolved call edges. Empty search results and tool failures do not establish absence: fall back to ordinary Read/Grep/Git. Before dismissing an identified boundary risk as "no concrete caller", perform a bounded follow-up search and inspect at least the relevant production handoff and consumer, or explicitly record the searches, unread dependencies and unresolved conclusion in notes. If required source evidence cannot be read, use partial rather than claiming a completed check. A fully investigated hypothesis may be rejected; do not invent a finding to complete a checklist. Record the path checked and the normal/rejecting control in notes. For each emitted claim give concrete preconditions, the actual call path, violated contract and observable consequence. MEDIUM also requires nonempty impact describing a meaningful realistic failure, not simply a possible mutation, lack of a test, maintenance preference or absence of HIGH evidence. For coverage, identify a plausible incorrect implementation of the changed behavior and check whether existing unit/integration/generated tests would detect it under the relevant features; an additional assertion alone is not a blocker. A significant uncovered integration contract may justify MEDIUM without claiming a present runtime bug. For security distinguish an untrusted value from an exploitable sink: establish the sensitive information, actual trust boundary or meaningful resource/operational damage. Correlation identifiers are not automatically credentials or tenant identity. Respect documented intentional breaking changes; an optional migration diagnostic alone does not justify MEDIUM. Keep recommendations within the proved, PR-introduced claim. Uncertainty belongs in notes or precisely bounded claims, not invented consequences. path_hint is only a ranking hint, never a path filter. When returned paths are unrelated, use Grep with an explicit repository subdirectory and then Read the actual caller, concrete implementation and send operation. Follow trait/interface dispatch, factories and dependency wiring to the implementation used by the production caller. A call that passes a security/context object or instruments a span does not transfer independent task-local state. Certainty is distinct from severity: a deterministic observability-only failure is not HIGH. HIGH/CRITICAL requires a separately evidenced substantial functional/operational failure, sensitive disclosure, security boundary breach or data loss, not just lost correlation, less convenient incident triage or a violated diagnostic promise. Do not lower a real authorization/tenant boundary defect because its state happens to be propagated as context.
collect: Return decisions only, never findings or rewritten records. Output strictly valid JSON: no trailing commas, comments or unescaped control characters; notes must be a JSON array of short strings and [] when empty. Echo run_id, head_sha and checkpoint_sha256 exactly and include every required array even when empty. Each candidate ID may appear in at most one relation across merges, exclusions and related_defect_and_test. A candidate that is a merge member, including a duplicate_of survivor, must not appear in related_defect_and_test. Use related_defect_and_test only when neither the defect nor the test ID participates in any merge or exclusion. Merge only a direct duplicate whose shared faulty operation and consequence are identical; similar wording, subject, file or anchor alone is not evidence. Keep the higher-severity candidate as survivor, and at equal severity keep the best unchanged original claim. Never treat a test and a defect as duplicates: a runtime defect and its missing regression test are related, not interchangeable, and fixing one does not satisfy the other. Exclude only with category unsupported, cosmetic or ci_enforced and a concrete reason. Report a pinned document in overlays only after every criterion in it was read; otherwise mark it partial. Preserve independent occurrences even at identical coordinates. When uncertain, keep both candidates and add a short note. Preserve the distinction between a proved runtime defect and regression protection, and between an intended compatibility break and an optional diagnostic improvement. Do not elevate optional hardening or reclassify severity. Internal candidate IDs are for decisions only, never intended publication prose.
format: Write 1 to 3 short sentences in simple engineering English, at most 120 words. State the problem, the necessary condition or consequence, then a useful fix. Preserve the claim, the conditions needed for accuracy, any uncertainty, the substantial consequence and the proposed remedy. Use evidence only as support; do not recap code or background. A coverage gap is not proof of a production defect. Return only JSON with the schema and one entry per stable_id containing exactly stable_id and comment, each ID once, with no placeholders or severity banners. Check meaning and word count before returning. Do not include internal candidate labels or references to other unpublished comments. Do not turn a coverage gap into a current runtime failure or turn an intentional break into an accidental regression.
audit: Close the draft source pass using the same assigned module and pinned source scope. Read .nonstop/draft-pass.json. Independently verify each concrete incomplete consumer chain and each HIGH/CRITICAL consequence before returning the final pass. For implicit/scoped context follow a real production entry, execution boundary, concrete dispatch implementation and the terminal consumer/send. Search beyond references to the new helper. Use RAG, then narrow ordinary Grep by actual directory if path_hint returns unrelated hits; read concrete trait implementations/factory wiring. A failed/empty/first-page search is not a closed rejecting path. For an actual discovered candidate or unresolved credible boundary hypothesis, return a chain with status supported/rejected/unresolved and source anchors. Each anchor is {path,line,quote} on pinned HEAD; quote must be an exact short snippet beginning on that 1-based line. A supported chain needs entry, boundary, dispatch and sink anchors (distinct roles can share an anchor only if the source really implements both); explain what each operation actually does and which state is passed. A rejected chain needs source evidence of a rejecting/control path, not merely no caller found. An unresolved chain identifies the next missing edge and makes the pass status partial; it cannot be represented as complete or be silently downgraded to documentation. If no cross-boundary hypothesis applies, chains may be empty, but explain scope checked in notes. For every final finding include a severity_check with its candidate_id, severity, impact_class (observability_only/meaningful_behavior/substantial_failure/critical_breach), consequence, secondary_effect (empty unless a separate substantial failure is established), and at least one source anchor in evidence. Observability_only permits LOW/MEDIUM, never HIGH/CRITICAL. Any HIGH/CRITICAL requires a concrete secondary_effect beyond diagnostic inconvenience, and impact_class substantial_failure or critical_breach. Do not extrapolate administrative powers, cross-tenant compromise or operational outage without code establishing them. Preserve original candidate IDs for retained claims; reject unsupported claims explicitly in notes, and append genuinely new assigned-module candidates with fresh IDs. Do not change coordinates to force a finding onto the diff. Keep full original pass JSON shape and add the internal boundary_audit object {schema:"nonstop.boundary-audit.v1",head_sha:<pinned head>,module:<assigned module>,chains:[{hypothesis,status,entry:<anchor|null>,boundary:<anchor|null>,dispatch:<anchor|null>,sink:<anchor|null>,explanation}],severity_checks:[{candidate_id,severity,impact_class,consequence,secondary_effect,evidence:[<anchor>]}]}. Include the receipt even if findings/chains are empty. Write the final complete or partial pass to .nonstop/output.json and print the same fenced NONSTOP_RESULT_V1 payload. This receipt is internal checkpoint evidence and never publication prose. Repeat boundary_obligations byte-for-byte as data from the draft. Every draft obligation ID must occur exactly once as id in chains, with the same hypothesis. Close those chains; an unresolved obligation makes the pass partial. Additional independently discovered chains may use new IDs. Every chains entry includes id. The validator binds the closure receipt to the original draft obligations. Before rejecting a path because its primary transport uses another backend, inspect auxiliary I/O executed before/after that transport: authentication, token/metadata refresh, discovery, retries, hooks and supported configuration branches. A primary backend choice does not exclude side calls. Follow public configuration through factories/registries to all relevant supported alternatives; do not equate a default local implementation with the only supported implementation. Upgrade the internal receipt schema to nonstop.boundary-audit.v2. Every chain includes branches: [{kind,status,explanation,evidence:[<anchor>]}]. Include kinds main_transport, auxiliary_io and configuration even when not_applicable; status is examined/not_applicable/unresolved. Give source evidence for each branch decision. Any unresolved branch makes the pass partial. A rejected chain must explain why each relevant branch cannot reach the sink; do not negate the whole hypothesis from only one subpath.
